51444-claudian-volume-2-of-2-with-an-eng.title: Claudian Volume 2 Of 2 With An English Translation By Mauric
51444-claudian-volume-2-of-2-with-an-eng.creator: Unknown
51444-claudian-volume-2-of-2-with-an-eng.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Thus far the warrior’s praise! Now let my gentler Muse relax the strings and tell by what virtues he governs the world, tempering fear with love, say what counsel moved him at last to assume those consular robes that cried out to him, and bestowed on our annals a year named after himself.

arxiv-1810-04986.title: An Efficient Data-Driven Model for Generation Expansion Planning with Short-Term Operational Constraints Thanks: This work was supported by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC) Discovery Grant.
arxiv-1810-04986.creator: 1 st Hassan Shavandi, 2 nd Mehrdad Pirnia, 3 rd J. David Fuller
arxiv-1810-04986.description: Abstract Generation expansion planning models have been useful aids for long-term planning in electricity markets. Recent growth in intermittent renewable generation has increased the need to model non-renewable responses to rapid changes in daily loads, leading research to incorporate unit commitment features into generation expansion models.

arxiv-2007-06134.title: Adaptive Periodic Averaging: A Practical Approach to Reducing Communication in Distributed Learning
arxiv-2007-06134.creator: Peng Jiang, Gagan Agrawal
arxiv-2007-06134.description: Abstract Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is the key learning algorithm for many machine learning tasks. Because of its computational costs, there is a growing interest in accelerating SGD on HPC resources like GPU clusters. However, the performance of parallel SGD is still bottlenecked by the high communication costs even with a fast connection among the machines.

arxiv-2109-12086.title: Running vacuum interacting with dark matter or with running gravitational coupling. Phenomenological implications
arxiv-2109-12086.creator: Joan Solà Peracaula a,b
arxiv-2109-12086.description: Abstract The cosmological term, Λ \Lambda , in Einstein’s equations is an essential ingredient of the ‘concordance’ Λ \Lambda CDM model of cosmology. In this mini-review presentation, we assess the possibility that Λ \Lambda can be a dynamical quantity, more specifically a ‘running quantity’ in quantum field theory in curved spacetime.

arxiv-2205-05070.title: Tensor-based Collaborative Filtering With Smooth Ratings Scale
arxiv-2205-05070.creator: Nikita Marin, Elizaveta Makhneva, Maria Lysyuk, Vladimir Chernyy, Ivan Oseledets, Evgeny Frolov
arxiv-2205-05070.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nikita Marin, Elizaveta Makhneva, Maria Lysyuk, Vladimir Chernyy, Ivan Oseledets, Evgeny Frolov. Conventional collaborative filtering techniques don’t take into consideration the effect of discrepancy in users’ rating perception. Some users may rarely give 5 stars to items while others almost always assign 5 stars to the chosen item. Even if they had experience with the same items this systematic discrepancy in their evaluation style will lead to the systematic errors in the ability of recommender system to effectively extract right patterns from data.

arxiv-2307-12200.title: The standard lens cluster in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} uniquely minimizes relative perimeter
arxiv-2307-12200.creator: Stan Alama, Lia Bronsard, Silas Vriend
arxiv-2307-12200.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Stan Alama, Lia Bronsard, Silas Vriend. In this article we consider the isoperimetric problem for partitioning the plane into three disjoint domains, one having unit area and the remaining two having infinite area. We show that the only solution, up to rigid motions of the plane, is a lens cluster consisting of circular arcs containing the finite area region, attached to a single axis, with two triple junctions where the arcs meet at 120 degree angles.

arxiv-2408-15173.title: Exploiting Approximate Symmetry for Efficient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2408-15173.creator: Batuhan Yardim, Niao He
arxiv-2408-15173.description: Abstract Mean-field games (MFG) have become significant tools for solving large-scale multi-agent reinforcement learning problems under symmetry. However, the assumption of exact symmetry limits the applicability of MFGs, as real-world scenarios often feature inherent heterogeneity. Furthermore, most works on MFG assume access to a known MFG model, which might not be readily available for real-world finite-agent games.

arxiv-2410-02220.title: Data to Defense: The Role of Curation in Customizing LLMs Against Jailbreaking Attacks This paper includes red-teaming information and content generated by models that may be offensive in nature.
arxiv-2410-02220.creator: Xiaoqun Liu, Jiacheng Liang, Luoxi Tang, Muchao Ye, Weicheng Ma, Zhaohan Xi
arxiv-2410-02220.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are widely adapted for downstream applications through fine-tuning, a process named customization . However, recent studies have identified a vulnerability during this process, where malicious samples can compromise the robustness of LLMs and amplify harmful behaviors—an attack commonly referred to as jailbreaking.

arxiv-2502-14159.title: Homological properties of the module of differentials
arxiv-2502-14159.creator: Jürgen Herzog Appendix by Benjamin Briggs and Srikanth B. Iyengar
arxiv-2502-14159.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jürgen Herzog Appendix by Benjamin Briggs and Srikanth B. Iyengar. These notes were produced by Jürgen Herzog to accompany his lectures in Recife, Brazil, in 1980, on the homological algebra of noetherian local rings. They are are concerned with two conjectures made by Wolmer Vasconcelos: if the conormal module of a local ring has finite projective dimension, or if the module of differentials, taken over an appropriate field, has finite projective dimension, then the ring must be complete intersection.

arxiv-2508-13578.title: Froggatt-Nielsen like mechanism in the framework of Modular Symmetry for Neutrino Mass, Mixing and Leptogenesis
arxiv-2508-13578.creator: Gourab Pathak, Mrinal Kumar Das
arxiv-2508-13578.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gourab Pathak, Mrinal Kumar Das. We study a neutrino mass model with Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) like modular symmetry. The FN mechanism requires an additional gauge symmetry, U ​ ( 1 ) F ​ N U(1)_{FN} , which is spontaneously broken at high energies. But in this work, we do not need an extra symmetry as modular weights play the role of the FN charges of the additional U ​ ( 1 ) F ​ N U(1)_{FN} symmetry.

pmc-10484940.title: Recyclable photoresins for light-mediated additive manufacturing towards Loop 3D printing
pmc-10484940.creator: Xabier Lopez de Pariza, Oihane Varela, Samantha O Catt, Timothy E Long, Eva Blasco, Haritz Sardon
pmc-10484940.description: Additive manufacturing (AM) of polymeric materials enables the manufacturing of complex structures for a wide range of applications. Among AM methods vat photopolymerization (VP) is desired owing to improved efficiency, excellent surface finish, and printing resolution at the micron-scale. Nevertheless, the major portion of resins available for VP are based on systems with limited or negligible recyclability.

pmc-10625288.title: sFgl2 gene-modified MSCs regulate the differentiation of CD4+ T cells in the treatment of autoimmune hepatitis
pmc-10625288.creator: Wenbin Ji, Weiwei Wang, Peiyuan Li, Yanhong Liu, Baotong Zhang, Feng Qi
pmc-10625288.description: BackgroundAutoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is a T-cell-mediated autoimmune liver disease that can lead to liver injury and has a poor long-term prognosis. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have immunosuppressive effects and can treat AIH. CD4+ T cells express the unique inhibitory Fcγ receptor (FcγRIIB), which is the only receptor for the immunosuppressive factor soluble fibrinogen-like protein 2 (sFgl2).

pmc-10640731.description: BackgroundTo research the effect of China’s many-child policy on the number of births and the prevalence of serious teratogenic and disabling defects (STDDs) in Hunan province.MethodsWe performed an observational study based on the Birth Defect (BD) Surveillance System of Hunan Province and chose STDD case cards. From 2012–2022, we defined the following 4 periods: the one-child policy (OCP) (2012.01–2013.

pmc-10717277.title: Assessing the impact of aprepitant and ondansetron on postoperative nausea and vomiting in orthognathic surgeries: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-10717277.creator: Mostafa Alam, Alireza Shakeri, Ardeshir Khorsand, Karim Nasseri, Sadaf Nasseri
pmc-10717277.description: BackgroundPostoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) is a common side effect associated with general anesthesia. Both ondansetron and aprepitant been effectively used to prevent PONV. However, there is a disagreement of opinions regarding the superiority of these two drugs. This study aims to compare the efficacy of aprepitant with ondansetron in preventing PONV following orthognathic surgeries.

pmc-11356015.title: Coccygodynia in a Long-Term Cancer Survivor Diagnosed with Metastatic Cancer: A Case Report
pmc-11356015.creator: Jung Hyun Park, Seong Jin Park, Dulee Kim, Jae Hoo Park, So Young Kwon, Konstantinos Dimas
pmc-11356015.description: Background and Objectives: Rectal cancer is considered cured if no recurrence is found during the 5-year follow-up period after treatment. After this period, patients often believe that the cancer is completely eradicated. However, in modern society, where lifespans have become longer, it is important to recognize that metastatic cancer may occur long after the initial treatment has concluded.

pmc-11561770.title: Synthesis of the Spirocyclic Imine Fragment of Portimines Using a γ-Hydroxymethyl-α,β-butenolide Dienophile in a Diastereoselective Diels–Alder Reaction
pmc-11561770.creator: Ze Kuang, Xiao-Bo Ding, Freda F Li, Margaret A Brimble
pmc-11561770.description: The synthesis of the spirocyclic imine fragment of the portimine family of marine toxins has been achieved. A densely functionalized key lactone-ester intermediate was assembled via a highly diastereoselective Diels–Alder cycloaddition, involving a novel γ-hydroxymethyl-α,β-butenolide dienophile. A Stille coupling was employed to install the vinyl group. Selective elaboration of the two carbonyl groups successfully afforded the spirocyclic imine fragment.

pmc-11565028.title: Data on whole genome resequencing of selected Malaysian rice accessions with opposing response to salinity stress
pmc-11565028.creator: Shahril Ab Razak, Rabiatul-Adawiah Zainal-Abidin, Asmuni Mohd Ikmal, Norfarhan Mohd-Assaad, Noraziyah Abd Aziz Shamsudin
pmc-11565028.description: The genomics and genetic information of Malaysian rice (Oryza sativa L.) is currently limited. It was necessary to conduct genome resequencing of these rice accessions exhibiting different responses to salinity stress. The sequencing was carried out using the Illumina NovaSeq X platform with 30× sequencing coverage to pinpoint variants between salinity tolerant and sensitive rice accessions.

pmc-12438776.title: Convergence of Phenomenology and Neuroscience in Autism Therapy: A Case Study of Exchange and Development Therapy
pmc-12438776.creator: S Bora
pmc-12438776.description: IntroductionThis abstract explores the integration of phenomenology and neuroscience in understanding and managing Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through Exchange and Development Therapy (EDT). EDT, developed by Professor Gilbert Lelord, focuses on restoring impaired functions in children with autism through principles of calm, receptiveness, and reciprocity.

pmc-12589065.title: A microbiota-based perspective on urinary stone disease: insights from 16S rRNA sequencing and machine learning models
pmc-12589065.creator: Yufeng Liu, Aoyu Yang, Ziyi Zhang, Chen Shen, Wei Wang, Xiancheng Li
pmc-12589065.description: BackgroundUrinary stones are a multifactorial disease. In recent years, the role of microorganisms in its pathogenesis has attracted considerable attention. Although studies have suggested that certain microbes present in the gut and urine are associated with the formation of urinary stones, the current criteria for stone classification are not rigorous enough.

pmc-13207166.title: Functions and Sensors of Smart Walkers From 2015 to 2024: Scoping Review
pmc-13207166.creator: Nicole Strutz, Hanna Brodowski, Stephan Schulze, Alessandro Scano
pmc-13207166.description: BackgroundEarly mobilization and mobility are essential components of the recovery process following surgery and trauma-related hospitalization. In addition to personalized support from physiotherapists and health care professionals, assistive devices such as walkers play a crucial role in facilitating safe and effective mobility.

pmc-13250979.title: Elucidating the Oxygen-Activation Mechanism in Nonheme MnII-, FeII-, or CoII-Containing MOFs Mimicking FeII/2-Oxoglutarate-Dependent Complexes
pmc-13250979.creator: Ziyue Huang, Yingqi Li, Xiaotian Zhang, Xi Chen, Jiawei Xu, Haiyan Wei
pmc-13250979.description: A Fe/Zn metal–organic framework (MOF) that mimics the FeII/2-oxoglutarate-dependent complex (FeII/2-OGDC) was reported previously, but its oxygen-activation mechanism remains unclear. In the present research, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to study this Fe-based system and its Mn- and Co-substituted analogues. We found that all three systems follow the general oxygen-activation chemistry of FeII/2-OGDC but show clear metal-dependent differences.

pmc-13353586.creator: Michael T. Lawless, Caitlin Wyman, Maria Alejandra Pinero de Plaza, Heather Block, Stacey George, Rachel Ambagtsheer, Malcolm Battersby, Alison Kitson
pmc-13353586.description: AimTo explore how community‐dwelling older adults with multimorbidity experience, enact and navigate daily self‐care using the Caring Life‐Course Theory to identify opportunities for strengthening self‐care and self‐management support.DesignQualitative descriptive study.MethodsSemi‐structured interviews were conducted with community‐dwelling older adults aged ≥ 50 years living with two or more chronic conditions across three Australian states and territories.

pmc-13383495.title: Influence of calcium hydroxide/nano-chitosan as intracanal medication on push-out bond strength of epoxy resin and bioceramic sealers: an ex-vivo study
pmc-13383495.creator: Khaled A Ghozi, Mohamed A Gomaa, Amany E Badr
pmc-13383495.description: BackgroundThe present study aimed to evaluate the impact of intracanal medicaments—calcium hydroxide (CH) and calcium hydroxide/nano-chitosan (CH/NC)—on the push-out bond strength (POBS) of AH Plus (AHP) and NeoSEALER Flo (NSF).MethodsNano-chitosan (NC) characterization was done using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS) and zeta potential analysis.
